title: Despair, the closed door
hookLine: no one despairs of Allah's mercy except those without faith (12:87)

cards: A father at home, waiting. In Surah Yusuf, Jacob has lost his son Joseph, and now a second son is held far away in Egypt. The Qur'an says his eyes went white with grief.

If anyone has a reason to close the door, it's him. Instead he turns to his other sons and sends them back out on the road: go, look for news of Joseph and his brother. Then he says the line this day is built on.

teach.h: DESPAIR NOT OF THE SPIRIT OF ALLAH.
teach.b: Here is what Jacob says, in Pickthall's words: "despair not of the Spirit of Allah. Lo! none despaireth of the Spirit of Allah save disbelieving folk." First, who is speaking.
Not someone with a comfortable life handing out advice, but a man whose grief has taken his sight, telling his sons to keep looking. You met his tears on day one hundred thirty-one.
Grief isn't despair; he wept and kept looking. Hope, in this story, isn't a mood. It's getting back on the road.
Second, despair is called a disease of the heart because of what it claims: this is beyond Allah's mercy. That's a claim about Allah, and in the verse it sits next to unbelief.

Third, a verse first met on day five hundred fifty-nine, and again on the day of fear and hope, which opens the door wider still: "Say: O My slaves who have been prodigal to their own hurt! Despair not of the mercy of Allah, Who forgiveth all sins."

People who have wasted a great deal, on themselves, addressed by name. And last, a look back over these diseases: arrogance, envy, showing off, anger, greed, backbiting, lying, heedlessness, and now despair.
Each had a cure: a correction accepted, a prayer, a hidden deed, a seat, enough, silence, a true sentence, a reminder. Despair says none of it will work.
The verse says the door stays open. And if the darkness ever turns toward hurting yourself, in the US call or text 988, any hour; elsewhere, local emergency help. Tell someone you trust.

how: Muslim teachers treat despair of Allah's mercy as a disease of the heart, citing Jacob's words in Surah Yusuf and the call of Qur'an 39:53 to those who have wronged themselves not to despair.

o: feeling sad or grieving after a great loss
giving up hope that Allah's mercy can reach you
doubting whether a prayer was done correctly

games.q: despair, the closed door — tap the pairs.
p: go, look for news of Joseph
none despaireth of the Spirit of Allah
despair not of the mercy of Allah

s: Jacob's words against despair come after his life turned out fine
he says them while grieving, his eyes white with sorrow, sending his sons back out to look.
Qur'an 39:53 addresses people who have been prodigal to their own hurt
"Despair not of the mercy of Allah, Who forgiveth all sins."
in the verse, despair of Allah's Spirit sits beside disbelief
"none despaireth of the Spirit of Allah save disbelieving folk."

games.q: you're Jacob. one son lost, another held in Egypt, your eyes gone white with grief. your other sons are in front of you. what do you do?
o: send them back out to look for news of Joseph and his brother.
go to Egypt yourself to fight.
games.why: he sends them back out and tells them not to despair of the Spirit of Allah. hope, in the story, is an instruction to keep looking.

practice: Let one hard thing come to mind, just one: a relationship, a habit, a diagnosis, a debt, something you've decided won't change, and hold it the way Jacob held his lost son, honestly, without pretending it doesn't hurt.

Then do what he did and send someone back out on the road: one small step of looking, one question, one call, one try. If you pray, you can ask Allah for help with it by name; if not, just leave the door open a crack.

wordCard.voice: Despair. Giving up hope of Allah's mercy; in Surah Yusuf, the closed door a grieving father refuses to close. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: mercy; in 39:53, despair is despair of Allah's rahmah.

carryVoice: Your line: never despair. That closes the diseases of the heart. Tomorrow, a new part begins: what adab means.
